title: AWS CWI Exam Prep in Houston, TX: 6-Day Course
description: Six-day AWS CWI exam prep for Houston refinery, pipeline and fabrication welders: Parts A, B and C, API 1104 or ASME, online or at your Gulf Coast site.
h1: AWS CWI Exam Prep in Houston, Texas: Six Days of Preparation for Refinery, Pipeline and Fabrication Welding Inspectors
html:
Houston is where a large part of America's process piping, pipeline and offshore steel gets welded, repaired and checked. Refineries and chemical plants line the Ship Channel, transmission pipelines fan out from the region in every direction, and fabrication yards along the coast build modules, vessels and platform structures for projects around the world. Job postings for welding inspectors on the Gulf Coast ask for the AWS Certified Welding Inspector more often than for any other welding credential. Atlantis NDT runs a six-day (6-day) course that prepares welders, pipefitters, QC technicians, NDT technicians and engineers for that AWS examination. The American Welding Society decides who is eligible, gives the exam and issues the CWI; Atlantis teaches the material and stays out of the scoring. To price it for one person or a crew, send a Houston CWI exam prep enquiry.

How the six days work for a Houston candidate

The course mirrors the exam. Two days go to Fundamentals (Part A): processes, terminology, joint design, welding symbols, metallurgy, testing, discontinuities, safety and the inspector's duties. One day rehearses the Part B practical, one day is spent inside the code you choose for Part C, one day is timed mock papers, and the sixth day targets weak areas and exam logistics. Each day is broken down on the AWS CWI exam prep course page.

Atlantis NDT has its US office in Houston, but the CWI course is not taught as a public class there. Someone preparing on their own follows it online through a study plan, reading, practice items written by Atlantis and an instructor who answers questions in writing. Where a contractor, fabricator or plant has a group to prepare, the six days can come to that employer's Houston-area premises instead. Nothing runs on a published timetable. The practice material is original and follows the subject areas AWS publishes; it never reproduces AWS exam questions, and AWS has not approved or endorsed the course.

The Gulf Coast welding economy, sector by sector

Refining and chemical plants along the Ship Channel

From Pasadena and Deer Park out to Baytown and Texas City, the channel is lined with refineries, olefins units, chemical plants and terminals. Plant piping there is built and repaired under ASME B31.3, the welding procedures and welder tests sit under Section IX, and the materials range from carbon steel to chrome-moly, stainless and nickel alloys. That mix puts preheat, interpass control, post-weld heat treatment and hardness at the center of the inspector's day. During a turnaround, hundreds of welds may be cut out and replaced in a few weeks, and the CWI on the contractor's or owner's QC team tracks welder qualifications against each joint, verifies material and filler traceability, watches fit-up and root passes, and accepts completed welds visually before they go to NDT by a licensed radiography or ultrasonic contractor.

Pipelines and stations

Houston is the commercial center of the US pipeline business, and the lines that leave the region carry crude, refined products, natural gas and natural gas liquids. For interstate gas and liquid lines, PHMSA's regulations (49 CFR 192 for gas, 195 for hazardous liquids) adopt API 1104 by reference for welding and weld acceptance, and pipelines that stay inside Texas answer to the pipeline safety staff of the state's Railroad Commission. New construction, tie-ins, compressor and pump stations and integrity repairs all need welding inspectors who know API 1104 well, from welder qualification by destructive testing to the visual and radiographic acceptance standards. Pipeline spreads move constantly, so many Houston-based CWIs spend weeks at a time on the road.

Offshore and modular fabrication

Yards on the Texas and Louisiana coast build jackets, topsides, decks, modules and pipe racks, both for the Gulf of Mexico and for export. Offshore structural specifications commonly call up AWS D1.1 for structural welding, and tubular connections bring their own fit-up and inspection problems. Module work adds process piping to B31.3 inside a structural frame, so a yard inspector may switch between two codes in the same shift.

Pressure vessels, exchangers and tanks

The region has a deep base of shops building heat exchangers, columns, drums and reactors to ASME Section VIII, and tank builders erecting field-welded storage tanks for terminals and plants. Section IX governs the procedures and welder qualifications in those shops, and inspectors there spend as much time reading procedure qualification records as looking at welds.

Bridges, buildings and the space industry

Freeway interchanges and river and bayou crossings keep the Texas Department of Transportation and its fabricators working to AWS D1.5, the bridge welding code. Hospital towers in the Texas Medical Center, data centers, warehouses and downtown buildings bring structural steel welded to AWS D1.1 and checked under the building code's special inspection requirements on larger projects. And around Ellington and the Johnson Space Center a commercial space sector has grown up; the AWS Houston Section has itself toured the Axiom Space facility at Ellington. Space hardware is mostly welded to customer specifications, some of them built on AWS D17.1.

Who employs CWIs around Houston, and what they want

  • Engineering, procurement and construction contractors. Owner specifications on capital projects usually require welding inspection by qualified personnel and name the CWI. Contractors staff QC departments with CWIs and add more for peaks.
  • Turnaround and maintenance contractors. Seasonal turnarounds create short, intense demand for welding QC. A CWI who can start on short notice and knows Section IX and B31.3 is easy to place.
  • Owner and operator QA groups. Plants and pipeline companies keep their own inspectors to oversee contractors, review weld maps and records, and audit fabricators.
  • Third-party inspection firms. Source inspection at vendor shops and field inspection for owners are often performed by CWIs; see third-party inspection in Houston.
  • Fabrication yards and vessel shops. In-house QC inspectors control fit-up, welding and visual acceptance before NDT and hydrotest.

Pay on the Gulf Coast varies with code knowledge, travel and overtime more than with the credential alone. For a comparison of welding and code inspector earnings in the region, read code inspector vs CWI salary on the Gulf Coast.

Picking the Part C code that matches Houston work

Part C is open book, and AWS lets you choose which book. Besides API 1104 and AWS D1.1, AWS offers aluminum (D1.2), bridge (D1.5), railcar (D15.1) and aerospace (D17.1) books, an ASME package in which Section IX travels with B31.1 and B31.3, and an ISO option. Along the Gulf Coast nearly everyone ends up choosing between three of them.

If most of your welding isTake this bookWhat it tests you on
Refinery, chemical plant or power piping; vessel and exchanger shopsThe ASME bookProcedure and welder qualification variables under Section IX, and examination and acceptance in the piping codes
Cross-country pipeline, stations, tie-ins, integrity digsAPI 1104Procedure and welder qualification by destructive testing, and the acceptance standards for visual and radiographic examination
Offshore structures, modules, pipe racks, buildingsAWS D1.1Prequalified joints, qualification, fabrication tolerances and the visual acceptance criteria

Use the edition AWS lists on your application; exam editions often lag the latest printing. Background: API 1104, API 1104 acceptance criteria and AWS D1.1.

The AWS Houston Section

Houston has its own AWS section, part of District 18, and its calendar is busier than most. Recent activities have included regular section meetings, a member appreciation and awards night, an annual clay shoot, a spring training evening on underwater welding and NDT, a facility tour at Axiom Space and a fall educational program hosted by Miller Electric, with local welding suppliers taking part. The neighboring Sabine Section covers the refining towns to the east. For a CWI candidate the section matters in practical ways: it is where you meet working inspectors and QC managers, where you find people who can confirm your welding history for the AWS application, and where word spreads about contractors staffing up for the next turnaround or pipeline job. Details are on the section's website, reachable from aws.org.

Where Houston inspectors learned to weld

Most CWIs here came up through the trades. The Houston area has a wide spread of training routes: community colleges across Harris County and the east side run welding certificates and associate degrees, private welding schools such as the Houston campus of ArcLabs train new welders quickly (ArcLabs hosted an AWS Houston Section event in 2025), and the boilermaker and pipefitter apprenticeships train the pressure and pipe welders the plants depend on. Those routes matter for the CWI in two ways. AWS lets formal schooling, including recognized trade courses and welding degrees, offset part of the experience requirement. And a documented apprenticeship or school record makes it easier to prove the welding-related work AWS asks you to list.

One Houston-specific trap: contract work. A pipefitter who has worked twenty turnarounds for ten contractors has plenty of experience but a scattered paper trail. Start collecting dates, contractors, sites, codes and a contact for each job well before you apply.

Booking the exam from Houston

When AWS accepts your application it sends a confirmation letter with an eligibility code. That code is what Prometric asks for when you reserve seats for the two computer-based papers, Fundamentals and Code Application; AWS says Prometric has well over one hundred centers in the US, and the Houston metro has several to choose from. The practical part is handled separately: AWS gives Part B at its own seminar and examination locations on fixed dates, and US applications for a practical session close about six weeks ahead. Look up the current AWS seminar and exam schedule for the nearest Texas or Gulf Coast session before you fix your plans.

Part A is 150 questions on fundamentals. Part B combines hands-on tasks using tools and specimens supplied by AWS with 46 written questions. Part C lets you keep your code book open for somewhere between 50 and 65 questions. AWS requires at least 72% on every part, and at Prometric you have no more than two hours on each computer-based paper. AWS lists its current exam and seminar fees on aws.org; to plan the whole outlay, including time off and travel, see the CWI exam budget guide.

Studying around turnarounds and twelve-hour shifts

Refinery and plant work in Houston runs in seasons. Spring and fall turnarounds bring long stretches of twelve-hour days, and pipeline and offshore jobs take people away for weeks. The online route is built for that. A workable pattern is to do the fundamentals blocks during a quiet period, carry your code book to work and use breaks to look up the clauses that apply to the joints in front of you, practice Part B measurements on scrap coupons and cut-outs, and keep the timed mock papers for the fortnight before your Prometric appointment. Questions go to the instructor in writing whenever they come up, so a night shift is no obstacle.

Six days at a Houston contractor, yard or plant

An employer preparing a group can host all six days on its own ground. Houston groups are often mixed: a contractor might have some people heading for API 1104 and others for the ASME book. The code day splits to suit. The practical day uses the company's own fillet gauges, hi-lo gauges, bridge cam gauges and real welds, including welder test coupons and production cut-outs, so the measurement practice matches what those inspectors accept on the job. Timing can be planned around turnaround schedules so people are not pulled off critical work. Each candidate still deals with AWS personally: the company cannot file the application, the experience record or the vision examination on anyone's behalf.

Eligibility and the vision record

AWS sets the experience requirement by education level. Finishing high school sets the bar at five years in welding-related jobs. Degree holders in welding engineering or welding technology need just one, other schooling lands somewhere between, and anyone who left before graduating needs longer. AWS also requires an eye examination recorded on its form, covering near vision and color perception, carried out by a qualified practitioner and dated within the period AWS allows before your exam. If your years fall short, AWS's associate-level credential, the CAWI, lets you inspect under a CWI's supervision while you build them. More detail is in the CWI requirements and career guide.

After the CWI: Houston career paths

AWS keeps a CWI valid for nine years, with renewal filings due at the third and sixth years. On the Gulf Coast the next step often depends on the sector. Plant inspectors frequently aim for API in-service inspection certifications such as API 510 or 570, which API runs under its own rules and which Atlantis does not train for. Pipeline inspectors build depth in API 1104 and integrity work. A good number also pick up nondestructive testing so they can run the ultrasonic or magnetic particle work themselves instead of waiting for a technician. That route goes through an employer's written practice: under ASNT SNT-TC-1A the company certifies its NDT staff once training and logged method hours are in place, and Atlantis provides the training (see NDT training in Houston and UT Level 2 training). There is a side-by-side of the CWI, API 577 and ASNT Level II credentials if you are weighing them. For local inspection work, see inspection services in Houston, ultrasonic testing in Houston and magnetic particle testing in Houston.

Other Gulf and Southwest CWI pages, and your quote

Candidates in the wider region can also read the CWI exam prep pages for Baton Rouge, Dallas and Tulsa.

For a price, tell us how many people want to prepare, outline each one's schooling and welding history, note whether they are aiming at API 1104, the ASME book or D1.1, and, for delivery at your site, give the location, the gauges and sample welds you have and any turnaround dates to avoid. Use the Houston CWI enquiry form; we reply within one business day.

faq.q: Is the Atlantis CWI course taught in a Houston classroom?
faq.a: No. Although Atlantis has its US office in Houston, the course is not a public class. Individuals take it online with written instructor support, and companies can host the six days at their own Houston-area site. See the outline.

faq.q: Who certifies me as a CWI?
faq.a: The American Welding Society does. It reviews your application, sets and grades every part, and issues the CWI to those who pass. The Atlantis course prepares you for that exam; AWS has not endorsed or approved it.

faq.q: Which Part C code should a refinery inspector in Houston choose?
faq.a: Most choose the ASME book, which covers Section IX welding qualification with the B31.1 and B31.3 piping codes, because plant piping is built and repaired to those documents.

faq.q: I work on pipeline spreads. Which code is best for me?
faq.a: API 1104, which federal pipeline safety rules incorporate for welding and weld acceptance. See API 1104 and the API 1104 acceptance criteria.

faq.q: Where do Houston candidates take the CWI exam?
faq.a: Fundamentals and Code Application are computer tests you reserve with Prometric, which has several centers around Houston. The hands-on practical happens only at AWS-run sessions on dates AWS fixes, so look up the closest one on aws.org before you plan.

faq.q: How do I prove experience if I have worked for many turnaround contractors?
faq.a: List every job with dates, contractor, site, the codes you worked to and a contact who can confirm it. AWS wants verifiable welding-related experience, so start gathering records early.
Seventy-two percent or better on every part. Expect 150 questions on Fundamentals, hands-on tasks plus 46 questions on the practical, and around 50 to 65 code questions with the book open.

faq.q: Can a contractor have the six days delivered around a turnaround?
faq.a: Yes. On-site delivery can be timed to avoid critical work, uses your gauges and real welds, and splits the code day by book. Send an enquiry.

faq.q: Does Atlantis train for API 510 or 570 after the CWI?
faq.a: No. API runs those certifications and Atlantis does not train for them. Atlantis does offer ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based NDT training; see NDT training in Houston.

faq.q: Are the practice questions taken from AWS exams?
faq.a: No. Each one is written in-house against the published AWS topic list, and Atlantis cannot see what is on the live exam. For extra NDT method practice, try the free practice tests.
